channel.title: Massachusetts and RI Lawyers Weekly - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Massachusetts and RI Lawyers Weekly (masslawyersweekly.com)

item.title: Administrative – Data sharing – Taxpayer addresses
item.description: Where plaintiffs have requested a preliminary injunction to prevent the Internal Revenue Service and Social Security Administration from sharing taxpayer addresses with Immigration and Customs Enforcement, that request should be granted based on the plaintiffs’ likelihood of success on the merits of their Administrative Procedure Act claims.

item.title: Civil rights – Ambulance – Cancellation
item.description: Where plaintiff parents brought suit after the death of their 8-month-old child, the defendants are entitled to summary judgment on the plaintiffs’ 42 U.S.C. §1983 claims, as the plaintiffs have not shown a state-created danger under the requirements of Irish v. Fowler, 979 F.3d 65 (1st Cir. 2020), nor have they have adequately alleged the level of conscious-shocking behavior sufficient for a Section 1983 claim.

item.title: Patent and trademark – Natural phenomena – Mental processes
item.description: Where a plaintiff has alleged infringement of its patent, the complaint must be dismissed because the plaintiff’s patent is directed to ineligible natural phenomena and ineligible mental processes.

item.title: Jurisdiction – Forum non conveniens
item.description: Where a defendant has moved to dismiss claims of human trafficking and conspiracy, that motion should be allowed because (1) an adequate alternative forum is available and (2) considerations of convenience and judicial efficiency strongly favor litigating the claim in that alternative forum.

item.title: Contract – Indemnification – NOAA assessment
item.description: Where (1) a defendant served as the master aboard a vessel owned by the plaintiff on a scallop-fishing voyage, (2) during the voyage, the defendant harvested scallops in an area forbidden under federal law, (3) the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) subsequently imposed a monetary assessment on the plaintiff and the defendant for that unlawful conduct and (4) the plaintiff has filed a complaint seeking indemnification from the defendant for the portion of the NOAA assessment

item.title: Insurance – Intellectual property exclusion – ‘Advertising ideas’
item.description: Where a defendant insurance company that provided commercial general liability coverage to three Massachusetts-based strip clubs has moved for summary judgment in a coverage dispute involving claims by professional models who allege that the clubs used their images in commercial advertisements without consent and without payment, the insurer’s motion should be allowed based on the applicability of an intellectual property exclusion and the inapplicability of that exclusion’s “advertising ideas”

item.title: Insurance – Duty to defend – Copyright infringement
item.description: Where the plaintiff, a real estate agency that has been sued for copyright infringement, filed a complaint seeking a declaratory judgment that the defendant insurance company has a duty to defend under a professional liability insurance policy, the insurer does have a duty to defend despite its argument that the copyright infringement claim is excluded because it is a claim of “misappropriation” or “improper use” of “other property.”

item.title: Education – Parental opt-out – Curriculum
item.description: Where a plaintiff was granted a preliminary injunction based on a likelihood of success on the merits of his claim that he had a constitutional right to direct the educational and religious upbringing of his child and had the right to opt his child out of exposure to certain classroom materials that include teachings that run counter to those of his religion, two books that are part of the child’s kindergarten curriculum do not fall within the scope of the preliminary injunction.

item.title: Immigration – Habeas corpus – Bond
item.description: Where a petitioner who was denied bond by an immigration judge has requested habeas corpus relief, that request should be granted because the IJ’s failure to consider whether alternatives to detention or other less restrictive means could address the risks of danger posed by the petitioner to the community was constitutionally deficient.

item.title: What Defense Strategies Apply to DUI Charges on Probation
item.description: Being on probation limits the freedom you experience, even if you're not behind bars. New arrests for driving under the influence while on probation carry much more severe charges.
